final_report.summary: Over 2 cycles, four mobile dashboard UX issues were fully resolved: (1) header row 2 made scrollable so Lock/Unlock button is reachable on phones, (2) overscroll-behavior-x: contain prevents accidental browser back/forward during horizontal column scrolling, (3) legacy broken scroll-dots replaced with numbered pill-shaped nav buttons ('1 Controls', '2 Analytics', '3 Activity') with proper tap targets and cyan active-state glow, (4) AtlasLab service status completely removed from dashboard HTML, CSS, JS, and backend config. Cycle 1 implemented all fixes (23/23 tests passed). Cycle 2 performed thorough visual verification using Selenium + headless Firefox across 375px, 320px, and 768px viewports (31/31 tests passed, zero issues found). A codebase-wide AtlasLab audit confirmed zero UI-facing references remain.
key_achievements: Header row 2 scrollable on mobile — Lock/Unlock button now reachable by horizontal scroll
Overscroll containment prevents accidental browser navigation during column swipes
Numbered column nav buttons (1 Controls, 2 Analytics, 3 Activity) with 76-84px tap targets, cyan glow active state, and ARIA attributes
AtlasLab service status completely removed from all dashboard code and backend config
54 total tests across both cycles (23 + 31) with zero failures
Visual verification via screenshots at 375px, 320px, and 768px viewports confirmed polished rendering
challenges_overcome: Investigation status HTML nesting was broken after AtlasLab removal — fixed by restructuring the containing elements
Nav buttons needed to be hidden on desktop while visible on mobile — solved with media query display toggling
Header scroll was borderline at some widths (scrollWidth only slightly exceeding clientWidth) — confirmed working via computed style measurement
lessons_learned: overscroll-behavior-x: contain is a single CSS property that prevents an entire class of accidental navigation — should be standard on any horizontally-scrolling mobile UI
Tap target sizing matters: W3C recommends 44x44px minimum; our 76-84x41px buttons exceed this for comfortable mobile use
Screenshot-based verification catches issues that unit tests and code inspection miss — computed style checks via Selenium confirm actual rendered state
Two cycles was the right budget: Cycle 1 for implementation, Cycle 2 for thorough verification with no wasted effort
Codebase-wide audits (grep for orphaned references) should accompany any feature removal to catch scattered remnants
